Reply naturally in English as the Patient to the last Doctor utterance.\nAnswer only the question, in 2–3 sentences maximum.\n\n[Dialogue]\nDoctor: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?\n\nPatient: I keep swinging between eating way too much and then trying to ‘make up for it’ with these harsh rules and routines, and it’s starting to take over my days. My primary doctor noticed this pattern and strongly suggested I talk to a professional before it gets any worse.\n\nDoctor: When you eat too much, do you ever try to get rid of the food by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?\n\nPatient: No, I don't throw up or use laxatives. Instead, the day after overeating, I force myself to go on long, punishing walks and restrict my food to just coffee and an apple. It's my way of trying to 'balance the books' and make up for what I ate.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time while feeling unable to stop, even if you do not vomit afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, that is exactly what happens late at night. I really don't think I've been significantly underweight at any point during this.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been significantly underweight, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range during this time?\n\nPatient: To the best of my knowledge, I've never been significantly underweight. My weight has just fluctuated a bit lately, though I'm not entirely sure of my exact range.\n\nDoctor: During the time these binge-and-restrict cycles have been happening, have you ever been significantly underweight or lost a lot of weight, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?\n\nPatient: My weight has mostly stayed in the normal range, though it fluctuates up and down. While I personally feel soft and pinch my stomach, my wife tells me I look fine, so I definitely haven't been significantly underweight.\n\nDoctor: Do your bingeing and compensatory behaviors ever happen in a way that is not clearly tied to your body shape or weight concerns, or are they mainly driven by fear of gaining weight and feeling overweight?\n\nPatient: They are absolutely tied to my body and weight concerns. Feeling \"soft and useless\" when I look in the mirror completely dictates my mood and drives the entire cycle. I only ever restrict my eating and force myself onto those punishing walks because I'm trying to control my weight.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been significantly underweight during this time, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure about my exact weight range, but it has just been fluctuating up and down rather than dropping extremely low. I certainly haven't been what anyone would call underweight during this time.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been significantly underweight during this period, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure of my exact weight category, but my primary doctor only noted some fluctuations rather than me being underweight. As far as I know, my weight has stayed in the normal range during this time.\n\nDoctor: When you try to make up for bingeing, do you ever use vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, or enemas, or is it only fasting, strict restriction, and exercise?\n\nPatient: No, I never use vomiting, laxatives, or anything like that. I don't believe I've ever been considered underweight during this time, though.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been significantly underweight at any point during these binge-and-compensate episodes, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure of my exact weight category, but my weight has mostly stayed in the normal range. My doctor only noted some fluctuations rather than me becoming severely underweight.\n\nDoctor: After you binge, do you ever have episodes of self-induced vomiting, or use laxatives, diuretics, or enemas to try to undo the eating? My self-worth is definitely tied to how I look; I often pinch my stomach in the mirror and call myself 'soft and useless,' and that thought alone determines whether I have a good or bad day.\n\nDoctor: Have you been significantly underweight at any point during this time, or has your weight usually been in the normal or higher range?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure about the exact weight categories, but my primary doctor just noticed that my weight has been fluctuating lately. While I personally feel soft and pinch my stomach, my wife tells me I look fine, so I definitely haven't been significantly underweight.\n\nDoctor: Do your bingeing and compensatory behaviors ever happen in a way that is not clearly tied to your body shape or weight concerns, or are they mainly driven by fear of gaining weight and feeling overweight?\n\nPatient: They are absolutely tied to my body and weight concerns.
